title: Module 5: Multi-Chip Distributed Training (DDP / FSDP vs. JAX Sharding) & Serving
description: Scaling across multi-chip TPU topologies over Inter-Chip Interconnect (ICI): AllReduce, ReduceScatter, AllGather, TorchTPU DDP/FSDP, and JAX NamedSharding / shard_map.

units.title: 5.1 Inter-Chip Interconnect (ICI) Collectives: AllReduce, ReduceScatter & AllGather

quiz.question: How is a ring AllReduce across N TPU chips mathematically decomposed into two bandwidth-optimal collective stages?
options: A ReduceScatter (where each chip ends up with 1/N of the summed gradient shard) followed by an AllGather (where all chips receive the full summed gradient).
Copying all tensors to Host CPU RAM and summing in Python.
Broadcasting Chip 0's gradients and discarding Chips 1..N-1.
quiz.explanation: AllReduce = ReduceScatter + AllGather. FSDP (ZeRO-3) exploits this exact decomposition by keeping only the ReduceScatter stage during the backward pass so each chip only stores 1/N of the gradients and optimizer state!

units.title: 5.2 TorchTPU DDP / FSDP vs. JAX NamedSharding & End-to-End Transformer Benchmark

quiz.question: In JAX GSPMD sharding, what does PartitionSpec('data', None) specify when applied to a 2D batch activation tensor of shape (Batch, Hidden)?
options: Axis 0 (Batch) is partitioned evenly across the 'data' mesh axis of TPU chips, while Axis 1 (Hidden) is replicated across all chips.
Axis 1 is sharded and Axis 0 is replicated.
quiz.explanation: Each element in PartitionSpec corresponds to a tensor dimension: 'data' shards dimension 0 across the 'data' mesh axis, and None replicates dimension 1.
